guide.summary: A sticky colony that stays in one place and builds a slimy film around itself.
guide.biology: Many real bacteria stick to surfaces and build a shared slimy layer, called a biofilm, that surrounds the colony.
guide.rules: Does not swim; lives attached to gel, sediment, stone edges, beads or mesh. Eats sugar first, then protein, using oxygen. After 10 seconds attached with more than 40 energy, it moves 0.05 body per second into its cell's film, up to 0.50 film per cell, stopping when its body is back to starting size. Film halves bacterial inhibitor exposure and dissolved flow across the cell's edges, and slowly turns into detritus. Recycler and Threadlace eat film. Prey for Amoeba and Siltworm, but Ciliates skip it; the only host of Lacephage, and only where film is at least 0.10.
guide.example: Place Velvet along a stone edge and compare how much film builds up with and without Recyclers nearby.
